Data summary of my five flux towers

Author

Matti Allgaier

Published

November 16, 2026

C1. Site overview

The five towers were downloaded with the FLUXNET Shuttle. The snapshot file fluxnet_shuttle_snapshot_20261113T162228.csv records what was downloaded. The data files are: AMF_BR-Ma2_FLUXNET_1999-2016_v1.3_r1.zip, AMF_US-UiB_FLUXNET_2008-2024_v1.3_r1.zip, CNF_CN-Zha_FLUXNET_2012-2024_v1.3_r1.zip, ICOS_IT-Tor_FLUXNET_2008-2025_v1.3_r1.zip, JPF_JP-Fhk_FLUXNET_2006-2023_v1.3_r1.zip.

Code 
my_sites  <- sort(unique(all_hh$site))
countries <- c(BR = "Brazil", CN = "China", IT = "Italy", JP = "Japan", US = "USA")

sites <- snapshot |>
  filter(site_id %in% my_sites) |>
  distinct(site_id, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  mutate(country = countries[substr(site_id, 1, 2)])

sites |>
  select(`Site ID` = site_id, Name = site_name, Country = country, IGBP = igbp,
         `Lat (°)` = location_lat, `Lon (°)` = location_long,
         `First year` = first_year, `Last year` = last_year,
         Hub = data_hub, Citation = product_citation) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)

Code 
world <- map_data("world")

ggplot() +
  geom_polygon(data = world, aes(long, lat, group = group),
               fill = "grey90", colour = "grey70", linewidth = 0.1) +
  geom_point(data = sites, aes(location_long, location_lat),
             colour = "red", size = 3) +
  geom_text(data = sites, aes(location_long, location_lat, label = site_id),
            nudge_y = 7, size = 3.5) +
  coord_quickmap() +
  labs(x = "Longitude (°)", y = "Latitude (°)") +
  theme_minimal()

Variables used. NEE, GPP and RECO are the _REF products. Where available, the variable u* threshold (VUT) and night-time partitioning (NT) were used. Where these were empty, the constant u* threshold (CUT) or day-time partitioning (DT) was used instead:

Code 
all_hh |>
  distinct(Site = site, `u* threshold` = ustar, Partitioning = partition) |>
  knitr::kable()
Site u* threshold Partitioning
BR-Ma2 VUT DT
US-UiB CUT NT
CN-Zha VUT NT
IT-Tor VUT NT
JP-Fhk VUT NT

Time stamps are local standard time (no daylight saving). They are stored with tz = "UTC" only as a technical container.

C2. Data coverage

Share of half hours per site and year in which NEE was measured (NEE_QC == 0) and not gap-filled.

Code 
coverage <- all_hh |>
  mutate(year = as.integer(format(time, "%Y"))) |>
  summarise(measured = mean(NEE_QC %in% 0), .by = c(site, year))

ggplot(coverage, aes(year, site, fill = measured)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white") +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(name = "Measured NEE", labels = scales::percent,
                       limits = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(x = "Year", y = "Site") +
  theme_minimal()

The best data come from US-UiB (on average 50 % measured NEE per year); the single best site-year is US-UiB in 2019 (68 %). BR-Ma2 has the lowest share of measured NEE, espacially in the first half of recorded years

C3. Summary statistics

Mean, minimum, maximum and share of missing half hours for each site. For precipitation (P_F), the Mean row gives the mean annual sum (mm per year); Min and Max of P_F refer to half-hourly values.

Code 
vars <- c(TA_F     = "TA_F (°C)",
          SW_IN_F  = "SW_IN_F (W m⁻²)",
          VPD_F    = "VPD_F (hPa)",
          P_F      = "P_F (mm)",
          NEE      = "NEE (µmol CO₂ m⁻² s⁻¹)",
          GPP      = "GPP (µmol CO₂ m⁻² s⁻¹)",
          RECO     = "RECO (µmol CO₂ m⁻² s⁻¹)",
          H_F_MDS  = "H (W m⁻²)",
          LE_F_MDS = "LE (W m⁻²)")

# Statistiken für alle Variablen und Türme
stats <- all_hh |>
  select(site, all_of(names(vars))) |>
  pivot_longer(-site, names_to = "var") |>
  summarise(Mean        = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE),
            Min         = min(value, na.rm = TRUE),
            Max         = max(value, na.rm = TRUE),
            `% missing` = 100 * mean(is.na(value)),
            .by = c(site, var))

# Niederschlag: mittlere Jahressumme statt Mittelwert
p_annual <- all_hh |>
  mutate(year = format(time, "%Y")) |>
  summarise(p_sum = sum(P_F, na.rm = TRUE), .by = c(site, year)) |>
  summarise(p_annual = mean(p_sum), .by = site)

stats <- stats |>
  left_join(p_annual, by = "site") |>
  mutate(Mean = if_else(var == "P_F", p_annual, Mean)) |>
  select(-p_annual)

# Eine Tabelle pro Turm
for (s in my_sites) {
  cat("\n\n### ", s, "\n\n", sep = "")
  tab <- stats |>
    filter(site == s) |>
    select(-site) |>
    mutate(var = vars[var]) |>
    pivot_longer(c(Mean, Min, Max, `% missing`), names_to = "Statistic") |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = var, values_from = value)
  cat(knitr::kable(tab, digits = 1), sep = "\n")
}

Note on precipitation. At US-UiB and CN-Zha, P_F is identical to the ERA5 reanalysis (P_ERA) in every year: no precipitation was measured at these towers, and the whole record is gap-filled from ERA5. The resulting annual sums (about 3,900 mm at US-UiB and 590 mm at CN-Zha) are roughly four times higher than the regional climate (about 1,000 mm in central Illinois and 100–200 mm around Zhangye). P_F at these two sites should therefore not be trusted. At BR-Ma2, IT-Tor and JP-Fhk, P_F is close to ERA5 and in a plausible range.

C4. Time series

Daily values were aggregated from the half-hourly data as the daily mean (µmol CO₂ m⁻² s⁻¹) and converted to g C m⁻² d⁻¹ with the factor 1.0378 (86 400 s × 12.011 g mol⁻¹ × 10⁻⁶). Days with missing half hours are left empty.

Code 
daily <- all_hh |>
  mutate(date = as.Date(time)) |>
  summarise(across(c(NEE, GPP, RECO), ~ mean(.x) * 1.0378),
            .by = c(site, date))
Code 
daily |>
  pivot_longer(c(NEE, GPP, RECO), names_to = "flux") |>
  ggplot(aes(date, value, colour = flux)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.2, alpha = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~ site, ncol = 1, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(GPP = "darkgreen", RECO = "darkorange", NEE = "black")) +
  labs(x = "Date", y = "Daily flux (g C m⁻² d⁻¹)", colour = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "top")

Check against the daily FLUXMET_DD file

Code 
z       <- list.files("data/raw", pattern = "JP-Fhk.*\\.zip$", full.names = TRUE)
dd_name <- grep("FLUXMET_DD", unzip(z, list = TRUE)$Name, value = TRUE)

dd <- read_csv(unz(z, dd_name), na = "-9999",
               col_select = c(TIMESTAMP, NEE_VUT_REF),
               col_types = cols(TIMESTAMP = "c", .default = "d")) |>
  mutate(date = as.Date(TIMESTAMP, format = "%Y%m%d"))

cmp <- daily |>
  filter(site == "JP-Fhk") |>
  inner_join(dd, by = "date")

ggplot(cmp, aes(NEE_VUT_REF, NEE)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.4, alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, colour = "red") +
  labs(x = "NEE from FLUXMET_DD (g C m⁻² d⁻¹)",
       y = "Own daily NEE (g C m⁻² d⁻¹)") +
  coord_equal() +
  theme_minimal()

For JP-Fhk, the own aggregation agrees with the official daily file: r = 0.9992, mean absolute difference = 0.039 g C m⁻² d⁻¹.

C5. Diurnal cycles

Seasons were defined from the month and the latitude of each site. In the northern hemisphere, spring is March–May, summer June–August, autumn September–November and winter December–February. For sites with a negative latitude (here only BR-Ma2), the months were shifted by six months, so that for example January counts as summer. BR-Ma2 lies almost on the equator (2.6° S), so its “seasons” are weak and mainly reflect wet and dry periods. Hours are local standard time (start of the half hour).

Code 
season_nh <- c("Winter", "Winter", "Spring", "Spring", "Spring", "Summer",
               "Summer", "Summer", "Autumn", "Autumn", "Autumn", "Winter")

diurnal <- all_hh |>
  left_join(sites |> select(site = site_id, lat = location_lat), by = "site") |>
  mutate(month  = as.integer(format(time, "%m")),
         # Südhalbkugel: Monate um 6 verschieben (Januar -> Juli usw.)
         month_adj = if_else(lat < 0, (month + 5) %% 12 + 1, month),
         season = factor(season_nh[month_adj],
                         levels = c("Spring", "Summer", "Autumn", "Winter")),
         hour   = as.numeric(format(time, "%H")) + as.numeric(format(time, "%M")) / 60) |>
  summarise(`NEE (µmol CO₂ m⁻² s⁻¹)` = mean(NEE, na.rm = TRUE),
            `LE (W m⁻²)`             = mean(LE_F_MDS, na.rm = TRUE),
            .by = c(site, season, hour))

diurnal |>
  pivot_longer(-c(site, season, hour), names_to = "variable") |>
  ggplot(aes(hour, value, colour = site)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +
  facet_grid(variable ~ season, scales = "free_y", switch = "y") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 24, 6)) +
  labs(x = "Hour of day (local standard time)", y = NULL, colour = "Site") +
  theme_minimal(base_size=13) +
  theme(strip.placement = "outside", legend.position = "top")

C6. My reading

Energy balance (JP-Fhk)

Only half hours in which both H and LE were measured (_QC == 0) are used.

Code 
eb <- all_hh |>
  filter(site == "JP-Fhk", H_F_MDS_QC == 0, LE_F_MDS_QC == 0) |>
  mutate(available = NETRAD - G_F_MDS,
         turbulent = H_F_MDS + LE_F_MDS) |>
  filter(!is.na(available), !is.na(turbulent))

fit   <- lm(turbulent ~ available, data = eb)
slope <- coef(fit)[["available"]]

ggplot(eb, aes(available, turbulent)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.3, alpha = 0.1) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, colour = "red") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", colour = "blue", se = FALSE) +
  annotate("text", x = -Inf, y = Inf, hjust = -0.1, vjust = 1.5,
           label = paste0("slope = ", round(slope, 2), " (n = ", nrow(eb), ")")) +
  labs(x = "NETRAD − G (W m⁻²)", y = "H + LE (W m⁻²)") +
  coord_equal() +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)

The slope of the linear fit is 0.71 (red line: 1:1).

Comparison of the towers

Code 
# Jährliche NEE-Summe: µmol m⁻² s⁻¹ × 1800 s × 12.011e-6 g/µmol = g C pro Halbstunde
annual <- all_hh |>
  mutate(year = format(time, "%Y")) |>
  summarise(nee_sum = sum(NEE * 1800 * 12.011e-6), .by = c(site, year)) |>
  filter(!is.na(nee_sum)) |>                       # nur vollständige Jahre
  summarise(`Mean annual NEE (g C m⁻² yr⁻¹)` = mean(nee_sum),
            `Complete years` = n(), .by = site)

# Jahresgang: Spannweite der mittleren monatlichen GPP (Tageswerte aus C4)
seasonal <- daily |>
  mutate(month = format(date, "%m")) |>
  summarise(gpp = mean(GPP, na.rm = TRUE), .by = c(site, month)) |>
  summarise(`GPP seasonal amplitude (g C m⁻² d⁻¹)` = max(gpp) - min(gpp), .by = site)

# Anteil lückengefüllter NEE-Halbstunden
gapfilled <- all_hh |>
  summarise(`Gap-filled NEE (%)` = 100 * mean(!(NEE_QC %in% 0)), .by = site)

annual |>
  left_join(seasonal, by = "site") |>
  left_join(gapfilled, by = "site") |>
  rename(Site = site) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
Site Mean annual NEE (g C m⁻² yr⁻¹) Complete years GPP seasonal amplitude (g C m⁻² d⁻¹) Gap-filled NEE (%)
BR-Ma2 -362.1 7 1.8 76.0
US-UiB -814.3 12 14.7 50.3
CN-Zha -651.2 10 10.4 59.9
IT-Tor -63.9 17 7.8 72.4
JP-Fhk -174.5 18 12.0 74.4

The highest carbon uptake occurs at the Illinois tower (US-UiB), which surprised me, considering that one of my towers is located in the Amazon rainforest. This could partly be explained by the high share of gap-filled NEE values at the Manaus tower (76 %) and the fact that only seven complete years are available there. What seems to be the highest carbon uptake is not nessesarily a proxy for the highest productivity because its cropland and the carbon (fruits) get harvested. US-UiB also shows the largest seasonal cycle in GPP. The lowest carbon uptake occurs at the tower in the Aosta Valley (IT-Tor), which could be explained by the short growing season at high altitude. At JP-Fhk, the turbulent fluxes (H + LE) account for about 71 % of the available energy (slope = 0.71), so the energy balance is not fully closed.
